title: Boolean Step Test Characterization
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $x,w,w'$ be Boolean lists, and let $s\in\mathbb{N}$. Assume that $w$ has the prescribed configuration-code length, its designated terminal bit is true, and the integer encoded in its input-position field is at most $|x|+1$. Assume also that $w'$ has the prescribed code length and its designated terminal bit is true. Then the Boolean step test on the configuration portion and input-position fields of $w,w'$ equals true if and only if the step-check predicate holds: $w$ is a valid configuration code, $w'$ has the required length and terminal bit, and some nondeterministic choice gives the prescribed input-head position update and passes the local tape-update check between the configuration portions of $w$ and $w'$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean symbols
the designated terminal bit of $w$ is true
the integer represented by the input-position field of $w$ is at most $|x|+1$
the designated terminal bit of $w'$ is true
caveat: The conclusion expands several codec predicates only by their roles; the definitions of the cell encoding and local scan check are not given informal descriptions.
